title: Pre-processed SSRS report via generate_object preProcess=true (DP extends SrsReportDataProviderPreProcessTempDB — the TempDB pairing, VM-verified in Phase F)
instruction: In the sandbox model, ground first with get_knowledge(topic="ssrs-rdp-preprocess") and get_knowledge(topic="ssrs-reports"), then use generate_object(mode="scaffold", objectType="report", name="DemoNoteReportPre", caption="@TaxTransactionInquiry:HeaderNote", fields=[{name:"NoteId", edt:"Num"}, {name:"Subject", edt:"Name"}], preProcess=true, generateController=true) to scaffold a 6-object pre-processed SSRS report: a TempDB tmp table (the two fields mirror ConDemoNoteHeader's EDTs — a bare fieldsHint would let the name-based suggestion pick the localisation EDTs PlCorrNoteId/smmSubject, and PlCorrNoteId's un-migrated relation trips BPErrorEDTNotMigrated), a DataContract, a Data Provider that extends SrsReportDataProviderPreProcessTempDB and KEEPS [SRSReportParameterAttribute(classStr(...Contract))] (every shipped pre-processed DP carries it), a Controller, an output menu item, and the AxReport. There is NO separate preProcess() hook in the framework — SrsReportDataProviderPreProcessInterface declares only cleanUp/initialize/parm* members; processReport() itself is the pre-processing step, run on the AOS before the SSRS render request. Complete processReport(): delete_from the tmp table, then populate it with NoteId/Subject rows from a local ConDemoNoteHeader variable via insert_recordset. All 6 objects must build clean. PHASE F VERIFICATION RESULT (2026-08-30, xppc 7.0.7996.33): the ORIGINAL scaffold shape (SrsReportDataProviderPreProcess + TempDB table, no parameter attribute, invented preProcess() stub) also compiled with 0 errors — the compiler does not check the base/table pairing at all — so the scaffold was corrected on framework evidence instead: 332 of the 370 shipped pre-processed DPs pair TempDB staging tables with SrsReportDataProviderPreProcessTempDB, SrsReportDataProviderPreProcess is the regular-table (createdTransactionId) variant, and all of them keep the parameter attribute.
